title: blueprint
description: The macOS blueprint wallpaper taken apart and rebuilt in layers: a blue ground, a canopy shadow, a grid of glass tiles, and the draughtsman's dashed marks around the thing being drawn. The shadow is grown rather than placed — two anisotropic noise fields, one for the leaf masses and one stretched hard across the diagonal so it breaks into branches, gated so the branches arrive in clusters the way a canopy actually hangs. It renders at a third of the resolution and a third of the frame rate, because softness upscales for free — which is the point: add ?bare to the URL, hand it to Plash, and the light through the leaves moves on your desk all day for almost nothing. The sheet is yours to reprint: ?hue turns the paper another colour, ?icon puts any mark in the middle, and the construction lines stop short of it, the way the original leaves its subject room.
